meta.name: Microsoft Power Platform App Maker Associate (PL-100)
meta.notes: Initial pack — 10 scenario-style questions across the PL-100 domains: app design, Dataverse data modelling, canvas vs model-driven choice, Power Fx formulas, Power Automate flow triggers for makers, Power BI + canvas integration, Copilot Studio topics, environments, sharing and DLP governance, and AI Builder pre-built models. Correct-option positions distributed 3/2/2/3.

questions.question: A citizen developer needs to build an internal tool that lets warehouse staff scan a barcode with a phone camera, look up the matching product in a small Dataverse table, and record a stock-take count. The layout must be optimised for a phone in portrait mode and use the on-device Camera and Barcode Scanner controls. Which Power Apps app type should the maker choose?
options: Model-driven app, because it automatically renders responsive forms on any device from the Dataverse schema
Power Pages site, because it is browser-based and can be pinned to a phone home screen
Canvas app, because it gives full pixel-level layout control and exposes the Camera and Barcode Scanner controls through Power Fx
SharePoint list form customised with Power Apps, because it inherits the SharePoint mobile shell
questions.explanation: Canvas apps are the maker-focused surface when the scenario demands device-level controls and pixel-perfect layout: the Barcode Scanner, Camera and Pen controls are all first-class canvas controls addressable through Power Fx, and canvas apps let the maker fix the screen size and orientation to phone-portrait. Model-driven apps derive their UI from the Dataverse form/view metadata and cannot host these device controls or lock a phone layout. Power Pages targets external anonymous or B2C users on public websites, not authenticated warehouse staff scanning barcodes. A SharePoint list form cannot host the rich device controls or a locked phone-portrait layout.

questions.question: A maker is designing a Dataverse table called Delivery. The table needs to store, for each delivery, a reference to the single Customer it belongs to, so that many deliveries can be filtered per customer and the customer's name is shown on the delivery form. Which column type on the Delivery table best models this relationship?
options: Lookup column pointing at the Customer table, which creates a many-to-one relationship from Delivery to Customer
Choice column whose options are populated by an Excel export of the current Customer list
Single Line of Text column that stores the Customer's name, kept in sync by a Power Automate flow
Autonumber column configured with the Customer prefix so the delivery id encodes the customer
questions.explanation: A Lookup column is the Dataverse mechanism that creates a many-to-one relationship from the child table (Delivery) to the parent (Customer): the maker gets referential integrity, the customer's primary name column is rendered automatically on the form, and views can group or filter deliveries per customer with no code. A Choice column populated from an Excel export goes stale the moment a customer is added and does not link to the Customer row. A text copy of the name loses referential integrity and duplicates data. An autonumber column produces a formatted string identifier but cannot represent a live relationship to Customer rows.

questions.question: In a canvas app, a maker needs the OnSelect property of a Submit button to write a new row to the Dataverse Issues table with the values entered in the txtTitle and txtDescription text inputs, and then navigate to a confirmation screen. Which Power Fx expression correctly implements this?
options: Collect(Issues, {Title: txtTitle.Text, Description: txtDescription.Text}); Screen(ConfirmScreen)
Set(Issues, {Title: txtTitle.Text, Description: txtDescription.Text}); Goto(ConfirmScreen)
SubmitForm(Issues, txtTitle.Text, txtDescription.Text); Redirect(ConfirmScreen)
Patch(Issues, Defaults(Issues), {Title: txtTitle.Text, Description: txtDescription.Text}); Navigate(ConfirmScreen)
questions.explanation: Patch is the canonical Power Fx function to create or update a row in a data source; passing Defaults(Issues) as the base record tells Patch to create a new row using the table's default field values, and the third argument supplies the changes. Navigate is the correct function to move between canvas screens. Collect writes to an in-memory local collection, not to Dataverse. Set assigns a global variable and does not write to a table; Goto is not a Power Fx function. SubmitForm operates against a Form control that is bound to a data source — it does not take field arguments — and Redirect is not a canvas-app function.

questions.question: A maker wants to build a Power Automate cloud flow that starts every time a new response is submitted to a Microsoft Forms feedback survey, then writes the response to a Dataverse table and sends a thank-you email to the respondent. Which flow type and trigger should they configure?
options: Instant cloud flow with the trigger 'Manually trigger a flow', launched from a button in Power Apps
Automated cloud flow with the Microsoft Forms trigger 'When a new response is submitted'
Scheduled cloud flow with a Recurrence trigger that runs every 15 minutes and polls Forms for new responses
Desktop flow recorded against the Microsoft Forms web page and scheduled through Power Automate for desktop
questions.explanation: This is the textbook use case for an Automated cloud flow: the flow reacts to an event in a connected service. The Microsoft Forms connector exposes 'When a new response is submitted', which fires once per response and gives the flow the response id to look up the answers. An Instant flow needs a human to press a button. A Scheduled flow with polling is wasteful, delays the thank-you email by up to 15 minutes, and would need extra logic to dedupe responses. A Desktop flow is designed for UI automation on a Windows desktop, not for reacting to cloud form submissions.

questions.question: A maker has finished a canvas app and needs to make it available to the entire Sales department (about 250 users). New Sales joiners should get access automatically. What is the most maintainable way to share the app?
options: Share the app individually with each of the 250 users and add each new joiner manually as they arrive
Publish the app to Microsoft AppSource so anyone with the tenant link can install it themselves
Share the app with the Sales Microsoft 365 group (or Azure AD security group), so membership changes flow through automatically
Distribute the .msapp file by email and ask users to import it into their own environment
questions.explanation: Sharing with a Microsoft 365 group or an Azure AD security group is the recommended pattern for medium and large audiences: the app permission follows group membership, so new joiners inherit access when they are added to the group and leavers lose it when removed. Sharing individually scales badly and creates a manual step for every new hire. AppSource is a public marketplace intended for ISV-published apps, not for an internal Sales department. Distributing a .msapp file bypasses the sharing model, does not enforce the same connections, and makes governance impossible.

questions.question: A maker needs to add a screen to their canvas app that shows a rich, interactive Power BI report — with slicers, drill-through, and tooltips — filtered to the currently signed-in user. Which approach is the recommended, low-code way to embed this content?
options: Insert the Power BI tile control and connect it to a specific tile pinned on a Power BI dashboard
Insert an HTML text control and paste the report's Publish to Web embed code
Insert the Power BI report control (formerly Power BI custom visual) and select the workspace, report and page directly
Add an Image control that points at a screenshot of the report exported to PNG
questions.explanation: The Power BI report control is the maker-facing, low-code way to embed a full report inside a canvas app: it is picked from the Insert pane, wired to a workspace/report/page, honours the report's row-level security for the signed-in user, and preserves interactivity — slicers, cross-filtering, drill-through and tooltips. The Power BI tile control only surfaces a single dashboard tile, losing report interactivity. Publish to Web is anonymous and forbidden for internal data because it removes authentication and RLS. A static PNG screenshot is not interactive and goes stale immediately.

questions.question: A maker is building a Copilot Studio chatbot for the HR team. When an employee asks 'How many vacation days do I have left?', the bot must recognise this intent and respond with the employee's balance from an HR system. In Copilot Studio, what is the maker configuring when they author this conversational unit?
options: A Solution, which packages the bot's tables and flows for deployment between environments
An Entity, which is a slot type that captures a piece of data such as a date or a number
A Skill, which is an external bot registered in the Bot Framework and called by name
A Topic, which defines the trigger phrases that start the conversation and the flow of authored messages and actions that follow
questions.explanation: In Copilot Studio, a Topic is the conversational unit the maker authors: it lists the trigger phrases the copilot listens for (like 'How many vacation days do I have left?'), then defines the ordered messages, questions and actions — including a call to a Power Automate flow to fetch the HR balance — that the bot executes in response. An Entity is a data type used to extract slot values from user input, not the conversation itself. A Skill is a separately-registered bot that a copilot can hand off to. A Solution is an ALM container used to move Power Platform components between environments — orthogonal to authoring the conversation.

questions.question: A maker starts building a real business-critical app for the Finance team directly in the tenant's default environment. What is the primary reason the CoE (Center of Excellence) team asks makers to avoid using the default environment for production apps?
options: The default environment does not support Power Automate cloud flows, so scheduled jobs cannot run there
The default environment is shared with every user in the tenant and cannot be restricted or governed like a purpose-built environment, so it is unsuitable for production workloads
The default environment has a hard cap of 100 rows per Dataverse table, which Finance data quickly exceeds
The default environment cannot host canvas apps, only model-driven apps built on Dataverse
questions.explanation: The default environment is provisioned automatically and every licensed user in the tenant is a Maker inside it — access cannot be restricted to a specific business unit or team the way a purpose-built production environment can. That makes it fine for personal productivity apps but a poor fit for a governed business-critical Finance workload; the CoE Starter Kit and Microsoft guidance both recommend a separate, appropriately-governed environment (with its own Dataverse database, DLP scope and admins) for production. The other statements are false: the default environment supports all cloud flow types, has no 100-row cap on Dataverse tables, and hosts canvas apps as well as model-driven apps.

questions.question: A maker wants to add invoice-scanning to a canvas app: when an accounts-payable clerk uploads a photo of a supplier invoice, the app must extract the invoice number, date, total, and line items into fields on the screen. The maker has no data-science background and wants a low-code AI capability that works out of the box. Which AI Builder capability should they use?
options: The AI Builder Invoice processing pre-built model, which extracts common invoice fields with no training required
A custom Object detection model, trained by drawing bounding boxes around each field on 50 sample invoices
A custom Category classification model, trained on the text of past invoices to predict a category
The AI Builder Sentiment analysis pre-built model, applied to the OCR text of the scanned invoice
questions.explanation: AI Builder ships pre-built models that are ready to consume without any training data — the Invoice processing model is designed exactly for this job: it extracts supplier information, invoice number, dates, totals and line items from an image or PDF of an invoice, and can be dropped into Power Apps or Power Automate via the AI Builder connector. Object detection is a custom model for counting or locating physical objects in images and requires labelled training data. Category classification predicts a class from text and does not extract structured fields. Sentiment analysis returns positive/negative/neutral scores — it cannot extract an invoice total.

questions.question: The tenant admin wants to make sure that in the Finance production environment, any Power Automate flow or Power Apps app can use the Dataverse and Office 365 Outlook connectors, but is blocked from using the Twitter connector — even if a maker tries to add it. Which Power Platform governance feature enforces this?
options: An environment security role granted to makers that hides the Twitter connector from the connector picker
A Dataverse role-based security profile that revokes the Twitter connector's privileges on Dataverse tables
A Microsoft Entra ID conditional access policy that blocks sign-in to the Twitter service
A Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy scoped to the Finance environment that places Dataverse and Outlook in the Business group and Twitter in the Blocked group
questions.explanation: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies are the Power Platform governance feature that classifies connectors into Business, Non-business and Blocked groups; connectors in the Blocked group cannot be used at all in the environments the policy targets, and connectors in different groups cannot be combined in the same app or flow. Scoping the policy to the Finance environment and placing Twitter in Blocked is the correct enforcement pattern. Security roles govern access to Dataverse rows and privileges, not the connector catalogue. Conditional access controls sign-in to Entra-integrated apps but does not stop a maker from adding a connector to a flow. There is no per-connector Dataverse security profile of the kind described.
